one_liner: AMD's AOCL build of FFTW 3.3.10 with Zen-tuned kernels, copies, transposes and planners; vendor claims beating stock FFTW, no published numbers.
what_it_does: AOCL-FFTW is FFTW 3.3.10 with AMD changes layered on behind compile-time switches. It keeps the whole FFTW 3 API (plans, guru interface, wisdom, threads, OpenMP, MPI, r2r, all precisions) and builds the same libfftw3/libfftw3f libraries, so existing FFTW code relinks against it unchanged. Extra features are configure options: --enable-amd-opt (master switch), --enable-amd-mpifft, --enable-amd-trans, --enable-amd-fast-planner, --enable-amd-top-n-planner, --enable-amd-app-opt and --enable-dynamic-dispatcher.
how_it_is_fast: The README credits improved SIMD kernels, a planner rule that prefers 256-bit AVX2 kernels (kernel/ifftw.h only allows 128-bit AVX2 kernels below size 1024), AVX2 intrinsic versions of the cpy2d and cpy2d_pair copy routines used by rank-0 and buffered plans, and an optional cache-tuned in-place transpose (Toms513-based) for large sizes. MPI FFTs get a block-based in-place transpose that overlaps memcpy with MPI communication. Planning time drops with a hash-table 'fast planner'; the Top-N planner stores the best three plans in wisdom to cut run-to-run variance; the application layer forces FFTW_PATIENT plans but caches them in an in-memory hash and a wisdom file so re-planning is cheap. Release 4.0 added AVX-512 DFT kernels and AVX-512 copy/transpose routines.
when_to_use: HPC codes already built on FFTW 3 (Quantum ESPRESSO, VASP-style plane-wave codes) running on AMD EPYC Zen 1-5 nodes, where relinking costs nothing and you can A/B test

Distributed in-place 3-D FFTs with fftw_mpi on Open MPI, where the AMD MPI transpose (--enable-amd-mpifft, optionally --enable-amd-mpi-vader-limit with btl_vader_eager_limit=65536) targets the transpose step
Applications that plan the same sizes repeatedly and suffer from FFTW_PATIENT planning time or run-to-run plan variation (fast planner, Top-N planner, app layer with wisdom)
Sites that standardise on the AOCL stack (Spack amdfftw, AOCC) and want one vendor-supported FFTW build
when_not_to_use: When you need a measured win: no repository page publishes a single number, issue #24 (Aug 2025, open, no AMD reply) reports stock FFTW 3.3.10 built with --enable-float --enable-avx2 --enable-avx512 was faster than this library built as the README says, and issue #19 reports it 'very slow' against MKL FFT on a Genoa machine
Intel or non-x86 CPUs: --enable-amd-opt only takes effect when configure runs on an AuthenticAMD host, and the kernels and flags target Zen; there is no ARM or POWER work beyond upstream FFTW

Thread-parallel single-node FFTs where performance matters: a search snippet of the ICPP 2023 GFFT paper (not opened) reports GFFT averaging 9.87x over AOCL-FFTW at 16 threads on EPYC, against 1.18x single-threaded
Projects that cannot accept GPL-2.0-or-later: the source is GPL like FFTW, and the verifier found Spack linking an AMD EULA for the prebuilt AOCL binaries
Builds with GCC through CMake with threads: issue #26 (open) shows the default ENABLE_AVX2 build failing because -mavx2 is not added, plus a link-order error

integration.form: static lib or shared lib (autotools or CMake); prebuilt AOCL binaries from AMD
integration.dependencies: none for the serial library; MPI (Open MPI assumed by the vader options) for MPI FFTs; OpenMP or pthreads for threaded builds
integration.min_toolchain: C compiler with AVX2/FMA; GCC 9+ to get -march=znver2, AOCC 4.0 / Clang 14+ for the dynamic dispatcher (configure errors out on older Clang); MSVC or Clang via CMake on Windows
integration.platforms: x86-64 Linux and Windows; AMD optimisations only on AMD Zen (Naples, Rome, Milan, Genoa, Zen 5 via AMD_ARCH=znver1..znver5); dynamic dispatcher is Linux-only (CMake stops with a fatal error on Windows); quad precision not available on Windows
integration.thread_safety: As upstream FFTW: fftw_execute* on distinct plans is thread-safe, the planner is not. With --enable-amd-app-opt, planning also reads and writes a global flag and the file wis.dat, so serialise plan creation. The Top-N planner is single-thread only (configure rejects it with threads, OpenMP or MPI).
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — same FFTW 3 API, symbol names and library names, so it relinks in place; but the AMD code paths compile in only with --enable-amd-opt on an AMD build host, several AMD options are mutually exclusive or restricted (fast planner vs Top-N, app layer not for MPI/r2r/long double/quad/split arrays), and the app layer changes planner behaviour

gotchas: configure reads /proc/cpuinfo: if it does not run on an AuthenticAMD machine (CI runner, Intel login node) or --enable-debug is set, --enable-amd-opt is silently ignored and you get plain FFTW 3.3.10

--enable-amd-app-opt overrides the caller's planner flags to FFTW_PATIENT, imports wisdom from ./wis.dat and exports new plans to ./wis.dat in the current working directory, and allocates a scratch copy of the input array during planning
Do not combine --enable-amd-opt with --enable-generic-simd128/256; the 256-bit-only switch (AMD_OPT_PREFER_256BIT_FPU) is incompatible with wisdom
Static libraries have had duplicate-symbol problems (issues #22 closed, #27 open, Mar 2026) and a 5.1 shared-library segfault on dlopen from Python (issue #23, closed)
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick AOCL-FFTW when you must keep the exact FFTW API and MPI/wisdom features on AMD EPYC and want the vendor-supported build; KFR, Admiral or VectorFFT have published single-node wins over FFTW or MKL but require a different API, so use them for new code where speed is measured.
verified_claims_summary: Nothing measured: the README and release notes only list optimisations (SIMD kernels, copy routines, 256-bit kernel selection, MPI transpose, faster planning) with no baseline numbers, compiler setup or hardware. The only figures seen are third-party search snippets (GFFT, ICPP 2023) comparing against AOCL-FFTW rather than measuring AOCL-FFTW against FFTW, and an open user issue says stock FFTW 3.3.10 was faster.
status_note: Active as AMD's AOCL component (releases 3.0.1 to 5.3; last commit 2026-05-19), but 5.2 and 5.3 say 'No major change', open build issues get no maintainer replies, and the code is GPL-2.0-or-later like FFTW.
